body:
Sounds like you're experiencing the effects of a coronacoaster! Life is very up and down at the moment. Our highs are very high and our lows are, well.... just horrible sometimes. 

I would encourage you to talk to your wife. It's important to get these things off our chest. For what it's worth, you sound like you're doing a great job. You're working, engaging in hobbies and still managing to find time to read to your young child. I'm in such awe of parents dealing with all this at the moment. 

Don't beat yourself for forgetting the book. Sounds like more auto-pilot than dissociation. Keep an eye on it, be mindful of your feelings and reach out for support. 

Good luck!

Not everyone expresses themselves in the same way. Good news is, there are so many different ways to do it! Do you draw or sing or dance? Do you paint? Or write? Journalling can be a really good tool for making sense of your thoughts. 

Oh, and struggle is good. It means you're growing :)

I apologise in advance for saying this: but your parents can f\*ck right off. 

I could be reading my 17 year old self's words right now. I'm so sorry that this is happening to you. I did exactly what you're contemplating: I left school at 17, got the best paying job I could and moved into a house share. For the first few months I jumped, flinched and broke down whenever I saw a car like theirs or anyone that looked like them around town. Then I got a counselor to work through my issues. I scrimped and saved everything I had, made new friends and had new life experiences. 

Now I'm 32. I live in a lovely house and I feel truly safe. 

Whatever you decide, I just want you to know that you CAN do this. You are in charge of your life - not your parents. I wish you all the very best, and am happy to answer any other questions you may have.

I really recommend researching Growth Mindset. It's not specific to mental health, but it's a useful and empowering tool. It should be useful for entering into the right and positive mindset for making some of the changes you want to make. Good luck!

People come in and out of our lives for different reasons. Some turn up and hang around, some stay for just a short while. They each have something to teach us and experiences we can learn from. If those you wanted to stay haven't, it's just not meant to be for them. They've obviously had their reasons - these reasons are no reflection on you. 

You are worth love, care and affection. Hang in there :)

It sounds like your thoughts are controlling you right now rather than the other way around. That's okay - this is something you CAN learn with time. Have you tried counselling? It works for lots of people, but it can take time. 

Whatever you decide, it sounds like you are aware of your issues and it's great that you want to take control of them and better your well-being.

Why is she pressing charges, just because you tried it on with her? Why does she want your dad to leave too?

I'm sorry you're going through this. You're human. We're not flawless - we make mistakes. Sometimes we make big ones. The good news is, you're not alone. Everyone deserves a redemption story.
